sentences.text: 1 The petitioner is a senior citizen and a widow of Late Dr.Devanandan, who passed away on 05.09.2014 due to the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident.

In respect of the accident,
O.P.(MV).No.1185 of 2014 was filed by the petitioner before the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Palakkad, which resulted in Ext.P1 award, granting compensation of Rs.38,02,377/- along with interest at the rate of 9% per annum till the realization of the award.
The insurer paid the amount during the month of June, 2018.

However, the insurer did not upload the TDS statement in time and therefore, the petitioner was compelled to submit her income tax returns for the assessment year 2018-2019 without declaring the interest income and the TDS credit thereon.
Ext.P2 is the return submitted for the said year.

Subsequently, the petitioner filed return for the assessment year 2019-2020 declaring the full interest income of Rs.12,14,147/- by claiming TDS credit of Rs.2,42,830/- based on the information furnished by the insurer.
Ext . P3
is the said return.

However, when the insurer uploaded 2025:KER:50883 the TDS statement, the TDS amounts were bifurcated by showing an amount of Rs.2,19,205/- for the year 2018-2019 and Rs.23,265/- for the year 2019-2020.
2. As a result of the same, while processing the return for the assessment year 2019, the petitioner was given credit of only Rs.23,625/- and the rest of the claim was rejected.

Upon realizing the above mismatch in the return, the petitioner submitted revised returns pertaining to the assessment years 2018-2019 and 2019-2020 to rectify the said mismatch and claim correct TDS credit.
Exts.P6 and P7 are the revised returns submitted by the petitioner and along with the same Ext.P8 application to condone the delay in submitting the returns was also submitted.
However, the said application happened to be rejected as per Ext.P12.
This writ petition was submitted by the petitioner in such circumstances.

3. I have heard Sri.Padmanathan K.V, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri.Harikumar G.,
learned standing counsel for the respondent.
4.

The specific contention raised by the learned counsel for the petitioner is that, Ext.P12 was passed without 2025:KER:50883 giving the petitioner an opportunity for being heard and without referring to any of the documents and the sequence of events that led to the situation where, the petitioner was compelled to submit revised return.
On perusal of Ext.P12, it was found that no hearing was conducted and also there is no reference of any of the documents referred to by the petitioner.
The learned standing counsel submitted that initially these documents were not brought to the notice of the officer concerned while passing Ext.P12.

Taking note of the fact that, the reason which prompted the petitioner to submit the revised return at a belated stage were not attributable to her and it was because of the delay in uploading the TDS statement by the insurer, I am of the view that a lenient view has to be taken in this case.
This is particularly because, TDS deducted is in respect of the compensation awarded to the petitioner by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal for the death of her husband in a motor accident.
5. In such circumstances, I am of the view that an interference is required in Ext.P12.

Accordingly,
this writ petition is disposed of quashing Ext.P12 with a direction to the 2025:KER:50883 1st respondent to reconsider Ext.P8 application, taking note of the circumstances that compelled the petitioner to submit revised return at a belated stage.

The petitioner shall make available the Vijayakumari.K.C vs Principal Commissioner Of Income Tax on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24160232/
2 documents that are referred to in this writ petition and also to establish the claim of the petitioner before the 1 st respondent.
Necessary orders in this regard shall be passed in accordance with law by the 1st respondent, within a period of three months from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment after giving the petitioner a reasonable opportunity to submit the said documents and hearing her.
Sd/-
